full_judgment: 2. In a suit for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from interfering with their possession the plaintiffs filed the suit stating, inter alia, that one Fariduddin Ahmed was the owner of 4.07 decimals of land of CS Khatian No. 5 of Mouza Shibrampur who sold the land by different Kabalas dated 15-3-1967 to Nazimuddin Maju Mia, Kashem Mia, Nabi Hossain and Khoda Baksh who were cousins and non-Bengali. During the liberation war of 1971 they were killed. Maju Mia died leaving 3 sons in plaintiff Nos. 1-3, widow in plaintiff No. 4 and daughter in plaintiff No. 5 as his heirs. Kashem Mia died leaving only one son, the proforma defendant No. 6 Mujahid, as his heir. Nabi Hossain, Naimuddin and Khoda Baksh died without any heir. They were all killed during the liberation war of 1971. In this way the plaintiffs and proforma defendant No. 6 Mujahid became the owners by way of inheritance and they are in possession of the suit land along with other lands. The defendants have no title and interest in the suit land and during the liberation war of 1971 the plaintiffs fled away elsewhere and taking this advantage the defendants got the possession of the original title deeds and other papers and created a forged deed in respect of the suit land showing Khoda Baksh as executant of the same. The defendants on the basis of this forged document tried to enter into the suit land on 10-5-1984 and hence the suit for permanent injunction.
